reviews.comment: Honestly the worst professor I've ever had. He just sucks at teaching. His lectures are useless because he rambles all the time. He reads off of pdf papers he wrote probably 15-20 years ago and has never worked on an example problem ever. He'll ramble about a topic for 25 minutes with asking for questions or realizing the whole class is lost.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: if only this professor did example problems everyone would understand. this class is one of the hardest within CVEN undergrad and Bracci has become complacent. just reading through pre written lecture notes every day, you pretty much have to teach yourself on this one

This man is not considerate of your time. He starts class early and ends late every time. He makes a point to let you know that he is a difficult grader and purposefully makes his tests hard "so you have to work until the last second." I seriously do not recommend him. You could learn the info on your own in half the time with his premade slides.

Dr. Bracci lectures with premade pdfs, explaining problems and concepts by reading off his notes and elaborating. I did not learn well from this teaching style. The course also has six (6) tests and a final (he doesn't drop any tests), work out homeworks, and book problems to make up the final grade. You have access to a lot of practice material.

7 tests, 7 bi-weekly assignments, and then 2 homework assignments due weekly. Tests were 2-3 questions, bi-weekly assignments were between 3 and 6 questions, and homework assignments were usually north of 12 questions. He has his notes already done and reads off of them during lectures. All-in-all. ton of work for meh lectures.

Bad at lecturing, doesn't provide resources for class other than the power point slides that he reads off of for the lectures, and is unreasonable with not allowing extra credit or accepting homework assignments that were turned in less than 30 seconds after the deadline.

CVEN 221 is not hard at all. He made it way harder than it should have been. He did not lecture. We had to watch videos and read the book. He said he wanted to teach us how to teach ourselves. There was a quiz every class about material that was due the following week with the homework. That means you had to be a week ahead of class to do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy
